gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $49.00 DDPAI N2 it called "best front + rear" is the front-only variant (the front-plus-rear N2 Dual is $89.00 on DDPAI's US store), or that 70mai's own US store has the M310 2K sold out, leaving Amazon at $39.99, the top of its 90-day range.
standout_why: Compared against Auto Roamer (cited), Guidespot (cited) and DashCamTalk's price tracker (cited), all opened 2026-11-21. Auto Roamer names no DDPAI, Rexing or onn model and gives the M310 only a 'mid-$30s to mid-$40s' street price with no date. Guidespot's only sub-$60 model is the M310 at $27.99 (July 2026), with no DDPAI. DashCamTalk's tracker has the M310 at $39.99 on Amazon, but its cheapest DDPAI is the Z60 Pro at $134.30. None prices the N2 by variant or reports the maker-store stock-out. Dash & Drive (cited) could not be opened (certificate error on three attempts), so it may hold part of this; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms the 70mai M310 as the front-only pick on price, but only via Amazon ($39.99 per DashCamTalk, against a 90-day average of $33.97), because 70mai's store is out of stock. It removes the DDPAI N2 as a front-plus-rear answer under $50: $49.00 buys the front camera alone and the Dual is $89.00. That leaves the onn set ChatGPT showed at $49.98 as the only front-plus-rear candidate, and I could not verify that price. For a row we can link, DDPAI's store has six variants at or under $50 with no record yet. The MINIPRO 2K + Hardwire Kit at $49.00 is the only camera-plus-parking-kit bundle I found inside the budget. I could not open DDPAI's spec pages (HTTP 429), so the supercapacitor, sensor and resolution claims that would justify a DDPAI row over the M310 are still unsourced. None of the five dash cams we already link is under $50 (the lowest is the DDPAI N5 Pro at $157.52 through our link).
